_comment: Maps a stuck object's own API group to the Deployment that owns
reconciling (and therefore un-stuck-ing) it, per
finalizers.py:classify_controller. Not the finalizer string:
finalizers.fluxcd.io and finalizer.managedresource.crossplane.io are
each shared by several controllers, so only the object's group tells
you which one actually owns it.
Each entry is {group, namespace, matchLabels} (an equality label
selector) or {group, namespace, labelSelector} (a raw selector
expression, for the rare case where any of several Deployments
servicing that group being ready counts as "running"). {group,
builtin: true} marks a group whose finalizers are removed by the
kube-apiserver itself, with no controller Deployment to check.
finalizers.py:classify_controller lists every Deployment in the
entry's namespace once (client.list_deployments, cached per namespace
for the check run) and matches matchLabels/labelSelector client-side
against each Deployment's spec.template.metadata.labels, falling back
to spec.selector.matchLabels. Never top-level metadata.labels: every
Crossplane provider package runtime Deployment in crossplane-system
carries none at all, and the Flux controller Deployments in
flux-system carry `app=<name>` only in the template/selector, not at
the top level -- a server-side selector against metadata.labels would
silently match nothing for either.
A group with no entry here resolves to controller status "unknown" --
an honest gap, not a bug: extend this file as real stuck objects turn
up in groups it does not cover yet.
Every entry below was read back from the live cluster (namespace by
namespace, every Deployment's spec.template.metadata.labels /
spec.selector.matchLabels checked against its group's matchLabels or
labelSelector) and verified 2026-09-28.
